title: The D-1 freshness contract, and the boundary bar the appender never revisited
verdict_reason: B-5R-E and B-5R-F are fixed in code, tested and mutation-checked, but only the requirement half of B-5R-E is live. The 16:20 refresh needs a scheduler restart, the boundary appender is OFF by default, and B-5R-D is unrepaired. Sequencing, not design.

part_a_freshness.diagnosis: one requirement was being asked of two data sources with different availability
part_a_freshness.why_the_daily_requirement_is_d_minus_1: RegimeLabels.get returns reg.asof(day - lag_days) with lag_days = 1, so a session on day D trades the label of D-1. Read from the code, not assumed
part_a_freshness.design_chosen: option 1 - split the requirement by data kind

options_rejected.option_3_split_preflight_state: that file is written by the SHARED 13:45 job and read by legacy too; re-shaping it is a much wider blast radius for information the new consistency check already surfaces
options_rejected.widen_the_requirement_to_d_minus_2: would trade a session on a label the backtest never used - a rule change disguised as a threshold

api.required_intraday_through: unchanged rule, for the parquets: prev trading day before 13:45, today from 13:45
api.required_daily_close_through: the last TRADING day before today, all day, for the daily series
api.required_data_through: kept as a name and delegates to the intraday one, because every existing caller means that one

holiday_aware.source: raits.live.trading_calendar where importable, reported by calendar_source()
holiday_aware.why: a weekday-only rule names the holiday itself on the day after one - a close no refresh can supply, so the gate would refuse for ever
holiday_aware.measured: the Monday after 2026-07-03/04 asks for Thursday 2026-07-02

new_check.name: preflight_consistency
new_check.fires_when: the pre-flight record says a day's 13:45 job SUCCEEDED and a data input still does not satisfy the requirement
new_check.silent_when: the pre-flight itself failed - a retry and a contract question are different problems with different owners

fri_1400_to_2359.note: the old gate asked for a close two hours away; roughly ten hours of every trading day recovered

mon_0900.note: correctly - Monday needs Friday's close and the file holds Thursday's

second_half_needs_a_job.why: the CSV gains D-1 at D's 13:45 and the requirement on D+1 is D; the 13:45 pre-flight is the ONLY refresh in the schedule

job.not_16_00: Polygon's daily aggregate settles a few minutes after the close
job.no_ibkr_refetch: the parquets were already brought to today at 13:45; a second fetch opens a second Gateway client for no gain
job.failure_is_not_a_preflight_failure: nothing today depended on it; marking the day failed would skip tomorrow's slots

inventory.classification: shared_infra - a legacy retirement cannot take the refresher with it

part_b_boundary.rule: a partial bar can only be COMPLETED, never contradicted

percentage_net.why: a cruder net for a bar from a different contract that happens to satisfy every monotonic rule; nothing legitimate sits near it

part_b_boundary.purity: boundary_replacement is pure - two frames in, one row out, no IO, no broker, no clock. A test parses its AST to keep it so, because a rule that only runs at 13:45 against a live Gateway is a rule that is never exercised

wiring.strictly_newer_filter: UNTOUCHED - the boundary bar is the one exception, not a widening
wiring.concat_position: between history and the new bars, so the existing ~duplicated(keep='last') prefers it
wiring.history_invariant: still requires every other bar in the 200-bar tail unchanged; the boundary timestamp is excluded BY NAME
wiring.verify: re-read the parquet and compare the replaced row; a repair that did not land is a failure

part_b_boundary.default: OFF (--repair-boundary absent from the scheduler argv)
part_b_boundary.why_off: it is the only path in that file that rewrites a bar the parquet already has, and the job runs unattended at 13:45
part_b_boundary.todays_1345_run: byte-identical to yesterday's - the new code executes, the flag is not passed, boundary is None and every path is the one that ran before

measure_first.safe_when: the Stress window is closed, after 12:30 ET

recommended_repair.why_this_one: it is the same code that will prevent recurrence when the flag is enabled in the scheduler - repairing with the tool that will do this daily is one rule, not two
recommended_repair.client_id_note: the updater's own, distinct from Track 1 data 89, safety 90 and legacy 1

part_c_mnq_sequencing.stricter_alternative: the scratch tool's --apply --expect <sha256> gate, if an explicit hash guard is wanted

live_without_restart: global_index/track1_freshness.py - every slot spawns a fresh child that imports it
needs_scheduler_restart: the spy_refresh_pm job - job definitions are fixed when make_scheduler builds the schedule
part_d_runtime.parity_while_neither_is_restarted: scheduler and mirror agree, because neither has it

older_tests_changed.was: asserted the OLD behaviour - Friday 13:46 must be stale
older_tests_changed.now: asserts the corrected requirement passes there AND that Monday morning still refuses

older_tests_changed.was: produced the refusing run with the CLOCK - at 15:00 the gate asked for today's close
older_tests_changed.problem: that refusal WAS the bug 5Q-5 removed
older_tests_changed.now: the refusing run comes from genuinely short data; the property 5Z exists for is untouched and its test was renamed from ..._two_clocks_...
60->61, 129->130, 100->101 and the shared-infra tables gained spy_refresh_pm

my_own_instrument_that_was_wrong.what: the purity test for boundary_replacement scanned the function text for 'fetch' and went red on its own refusal message 'not_offered: the fetch does not cover ...'
my_own_instrument_that_was_wrong.count: the FOURTH substring-over-prose test across these stages
my_own_instrument_that_was_wrong.fix: parses the AST and asserts the set of called names is disjoint from the IO names, with no imports inside the function

unrepaired; measure then one approved command
